## Runtime convention

All course scripts are meant to run inside the Docker image that contains the required tool. The script contains the analysis logic; the Docker command only chooses the software environment and mounts the project folder:

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  -w /work \
  docker.io/fgualdr/ngs-fastqc:latest \
  bash scripts/day1/01_fastqc_raw.sh
```

## Why this matters

The image provides software. The mounted project folder provides persistent files. `docker run --rm` starts a temporary container, runs the script inside `/work`, writes outputs into the mounted project folder, and removes the container when the command finishes. This separation makes the analysis portable across macOS, Linux, and Windows WSL2.

## Practical limits

Use two threads by default:

```bash
THREADS=2
```

More threads can overload student laptops and make failures harder to debug.
